findings.reason: if §2's restructure is measured through the wrapper rather than through the program object, the per-trip number it banks is the wrapper's overhead rather than the trip's, and the plan should name which entry the millisecond figures are taken on.
findings.text: `solve_reduced_newton_compiled` is a public per-call entry that forwards to a cached program and `_compiled_result`, so the interface a caller sees (one call) is separated from the object that carries the depth (the cached `ReducedProgram`); §2's design adds restructure on top of this wrapper without deciding whether §2's new callers hold the program directly — and the plan's own receipt f-20260909T1610 measured exactly this entry at 1.39–1.72× the direct-dispatch wall when it derived coordinates before the cache lookup, so the wrapper-with-a-cost shape is already demonstrated here

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; the §2 restructure lives inside `nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py` behind the single compiled entry `solve_reduced_newton_compiled`, which hides the program cache, the host fallback and the traced-argument plumbing behind one call.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan re-implements no shared owner; the one duplicate it did produce, `_requalify_krylov_step`'s hand copy of the conditioning policy in `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py`, was found by its own review and both call sites routed through the single `_apply_krylov_conditioning` helper.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan extends the existing solver rather than adding a subsystem: `nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py` reuses `fixed_point`'s settled exit and incumbent-mask acceptance (its module docstring, line 20), §3 consumes the accuracy certificate from `gs-absolute-accuracy-gates`, and its figures render through `nova.media`; I searched `nova/equilibrium` for the exit, per-trip and compiled mechanisms §1–§3 touch and found no independent reimplementation.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's compiled route adds a public per-call entry over the compiled program without stating why the program object cannot be the caller's route, and the plan's own history shows this entry is where a passthrough reappears.
